fullPassage:
Art & Our Environment

While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. Let us take a look at a few modern artworks that address environmental issues.

The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks rally people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to highlight the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.

He says, "You can't order a product online without having it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, made of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue because at the end of the day, you know, companies and governments can't ignore the interest of the consumers. At the same time, we also need to pressure governments and corporations to do the right thing."

The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. They are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more acidic. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will dissolve.

Kendler says, "I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage collective action and collective responsibility. One thing that art can do really well is to help us imagine how the world might be otherwise. Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it."

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to appreciate the world around them. "I believe we've separated ourselves from nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it," says Ching.

One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another. "I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. My call to action is to remember the magic and wonder of this planet."

Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, ring especially true in this context. "They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself."

Banksy's New Work in Port Talbot

Secretive street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth. When you look around the corner, however, you realize that the child's mouth is open to ash coming from a dumpster fire.

Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot resident, to create art that would highlight Port Talbot's dust problem. Owen believed that the area's children were facing serious health risks by playing in the dust coming from the local steel plant.

Children are particularly defenseless against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 93% of the world's children under 15 breathe in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even estimated that about 600,000 children died from exposure to polluted air.

Banksy's art has included environmental messages before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a child with a can of red paint and the words, "I remember when all this was trees."

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a (A)[spirited / spiritless] reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our (B)[surroundings / surfaces]. That is why art has played an (C)[essential / accidental] role in addressing social and global issues throughout history.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 예술은 대중으로부터 격렬한 반응을 끌어낼 수 있다. 우리의 주변을 바라보는 방식을 바꿀 수 있다. 예술은 필수적인 역할을 해 왔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① spirited — surroundings — essential
❌ ② spiritless — surfaces — essential
❌ ③ spirited — surfaces — accidental
❌ ④ spiritless — surroundings — accidental
✅ (A) spirited: '격렬한, 활기찬' 반응. spiritless(기운 없는)는 반대 의미. ✅ (B) surroundings: '주변 환경'. surfaces(표면)는 맥락과 무관. ✅ (C) essential: '필수적인'. accidental(우연한)은 의도적 역할과 반대.
det.tip: spirited(활기찬) ↔ spiritless(기운 없는). surroundings = '주변 환경'. essential = '필수적인'.

questions.passage: Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to (A)[opt out / opt in]. Of course, you can choose not to (B)[purchase / produce] products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to (C)[inform / ignore] your friends and family of the issue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 개인 소비자는 빠져나오기가 점점 더 어렵다. 플라스틱이 들어 있는 제품을 구매하지 않을 수 있다. 친구와 가족에게 문제를 알리는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① opt in — purchase — inform
✅ ② opt out — purchase — inform
❌ ③ opt out — produce — ignore
❌ ④ opt in — produce — ignore
✅ (A) opt out: '빠져나오다, 탈퇴하다'. opt in(참여하다)은 반대 의미. ✅ (B) purchase: '구매하다'. produce(생산하다)는 소비자 맥락에 부적절. ✅ (C) inform: '알리다'. ignore(무시하다)는 문제 해결 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: opt out(빠져나오다) ↔ opt in(참여하다). purchase(구매) ↔ produce(생산).

questions.passage: She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels (A)[carelessly / carefully]. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more (B)[acidic / alkaline]. I wanted to inspire people to raise their own (C)[awareness / indifference] about what they can actually do as individuals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 화석 연료를 무분별하게 태우면 바다 생물이 겪을 일. 바다는 점점 더 산성이 된다. 사람들의 인식을 일깨우고 싶었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① carefully — acidic — awareness
❌ ② carelessly — alkaline — indifference
✅ ③ carelessly — acidic — awareness
❌ ④ carefully — alkaline — indifference
✅ (A) carelessly: '무분별하게'. carefully(조심스럽게)는 환경 파괴 맥락과 반대. ✅ (B) acidic: '산성의'. alkaline(알칼리성의)은 CO2 흡수 결과와 반대. ✅ (C) awareness: '인식, 자각'. indifference(무관심)는 고무(inspire) 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: carelessly(무분별하게) ↔ carefully(조심스럽게). acidic(산성의) ↔ alkaline(알칼리성의). awareness(인식) ↔ indifference(무관심).

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An ①<u>excellent</u> artistic piece can communicate a message to us. That is why art has played an essential role in ②<u>addressing</u> social and global issues. His artworks ③<u>rally</u> people around environmental actions. He tries to ④<u>conceal</u> the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①뛰어난 예술 작품은 메시지를 전할 수 있다. ②다루는 데 필수적인 역할. 사람들을 환경 행동에 ③집결시킨다. 사실을 ④숨기려고 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① excellent: 원문 그대로. 뛰어난 예술 작품. ✅ ② addressing: 원문 그대로. 문제를 다루다. ✅ ③ rally: 원문 그대로. 사람들을 집결시키다. ❌ ④ conceal → highlight: 사실을 '강조하다'가 맞음. conceal(숨기다)은 반대 의미.
det.tip: highlight(강조하다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). rally = '집결시키다, 결집시키다'.

questions.passage: She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to ①<u>collect</u>. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. They are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth ②<u>dissolve</u> in acid. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels ③<u>carelessly</u>. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will ④<u>harden</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①모으는 데 1년이 걸렸다. 유치를 산에 ②녹일 때. 화석 연료를 ③무분별하게 태우면. 껍질이 ④굳어질 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① collect: 원문 그대로. 조개껍질을 모으다. ✅ ② dissolve: 원문 그대로. 산에 녹이다. ✅ ③ carelessly: 원문 그대로. 무분별하게. ❌ ④ harden → dissolve: 산성 바다에서 껍질은 '녹는다'. harden(굳어지다)은 반대 의미.
det.tip: dissolve(녹다) ↔ harden(굳어지다). 바다 산성화로 해양 생물의 껍질이 녹는다는 맥락.

questions.passage: I've been using my work as a means of ①<u>commenting</u> on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just ②<u>reflect</u> on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is ③<u>connected</u> and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great ④<u>obstacle</u> by inspiring us to take action.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사안을 ①비평하는 수단. 잘못된 것을 ②깊이 생각하다. 모든 것이 ③연결되어 있다. 큰 ④장애물을 만들 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① commenting: 원문 그대로. 사안에 대해 비평하다. ✅ ② reflect: 원문 그대로. 깊이 생각하다. ✅ ③ connected: 원문 그대로. 연결되어 있다. ❌ ④ obstacle → difference: 'make a great difference'(큰 변화를 만들다)가 원문. obstacle(장애물)은 긍정적 맥락과 부적합.
det.tip: make a great difference(큰 변화를 만들다). obstacle(장애물) ≠ difference(변화, 차이). silver lining = '어두운 상황 속 밝은 면'.

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can __________ a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. Let us take a look at a few modern artworks that address environmental issues. The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뛰어난 예술 작품은 우리에게 메시지를 전해 줄 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① distribute
✅ ② communicate
❌ ③ eliminate
❌ ④ memorize
✅ communicate: '전달하다, 소통하다'. 메시지를 전한다는 원문 의미. ❌ distribute(배포하다): 메시지 전달과 다른 뉘앙스. ❌ eliminate(제거하다): 반대 의미. ❌ memorize(암기하다): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: communicate a message = '메시지를 전달하다'. communicate는 '소통하다' 외에 '전하다'의 뜻도 있음.

questions.passage: You can't order a product online without having it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, made of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to __________. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 플라스틱에 대한 의존이 공급망에 내재되어 있어서 개인 소비자는 빠져나오기가 점점 더 어렵다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① give in
❌ ② sign up
✅ ③ opt out
❌ ④ break down
✅ opt out: '빠져나오다, 선택 해제하다'. 공급망에 내재된 플라스틱 의존에서 벗어나기 어렵다는 맥락. ❌ give in(굴복하다): 포기가 아닌 이탈의 맥락. ❌ sign up(등록하다): 반대 방향. ❌ break down(고장나다): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: opt out(빠져나오다) ↔ opt in(참여하다). 'opt out of ~'에서 벗어나다.

questions.passage: She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more acidic. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will dissolve. I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage __________ action and shared responsibility.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개인으로서 할 수 있는 일의 인식을 높이되, 동시에 공동의 행동과 공동의 책임감을 북돋우고 싶었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① collective
❌ ② selective
❌ ③ destructive
❌ ④ protective
✅ collective: '공동의, 집단적인'. 개인(individuals)과 대조를 이루는 집단적 행동. ❌ selective(선택적인): 책임감과 어울리지 않음. ❌ destructive(파괴적인): 긍정적 맥락과 반대. ❌ protective(보호적인): collective responsibility와 병렬이 안 됨.
det.tip: collective(공동의, 집단적인) ↔ individual(개인의). collective action = '공동 행동'.

questions.passage: The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks <u>rally</u> people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to highlight the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 rally와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그의 예술 작품들은 사람들이 환경 행동에 나서도록 집결시킨다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① scatter
❌ ② discourage
❌ ③ divide
✅ ④ mobilize
✅ mobilize: '동원하다, 결집시키다'. rally와 유사하게 사람들을 한데 모아 행동하게 하는 의미. ❌ scatter(흩뿌리다): 반의어. ❌ discourage(낙담시키다): 반대 방향. ❌ divide(나누다): 반의어.
det.tip: rally = '결집시키다, 규합하다'. mobilize = '동원하다'. 둘 다 사람들을 모아 행동하게 한다는 의미.

questions.passage: The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to <u>appreciate</u> the world around them. "I believe we've separated ourselves from nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it," says Ching.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 appreciate와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 인간들에게 주위 세상에 고마워하라는 조용한 호소.
det.analysis:
❌ ① neglect
✅ ② value
❌ ③ exploit
❌ ④ underestimate
✅ value: '소중히 여기다, 가치를 두다'. appreciate와 유사하게 감사하고 소중히 여기는 의미. ❌ neglect(무시하다): 반의어. ❌ exploit(착취하다): 부정적 의미. ❌ underestimate(과소평가하다): 반대 방향.
det.tip: appreciate = '감사하다, 가치를 인정하다'. value = '소중히 여기다'. 둘 다 긍정적 평가의 뜻.

questions.passage: One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another. I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just <u>reflect on</u> what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 reflect on과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 잘못된 것을 깊이 생각하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① glance at
❌ ② act on
✅ ③ think deeply about
❌ ④ contribute to
✅ think deeply about: '~에 대해 깊이 생각하다'. reflect on은 단순히 보는 것이 아니라 깊이 성찰하는 의미. ❌ glance at(흘깃 보다): 피상적 관찰. ❌ act on(~에 따라 행동하다): 행동 관련. ❌ contribute to(기여하다): 다른 의미.
det.tip: reflect on = '~을 깊이 생각하다, 성찰하다'. 거울(reflect)처럼 자신을 되돌아보는 이미지.

questions.passage: <u>Secretive</u> street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth. When you look around the corner, however, you realize that the child's mouth is open to ash coming from a dumpster fire.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 Secretive와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 비밀스러운 거리 예술가 Banksy.
det.analysis:
✅ ① open
❌ ② hidden
❌ ③ mysterious
❌ ④ reserved
✅ open: '개방적인, 공개적인'. secretive(비밀스러운)의 반의어. ❌ hidden(숨겨진): 유의어. ❌ mysterious(신비로운): 유사 의미. ❌ reserved(과묵한): 유사 방향.
det.tip: secretive(비밀스러운) ↔ open(개방적인). secretive는 정보를 숨기려는 성향.

questions.passage: Children are particularly <u>defenseless</u> against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 93% of the world's children under 15 breathe in toxic air every day.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 defenseless와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 어린이들은 대기 오염에 특히 무방비 상태이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① vulnerable
❌ ② helpless
❌ ③ exposed
✅ ④ protected
✅ protected: '보호받는'. defenseless(무방비의)의 정확한 반의어. ❌ vulnerable(취약한): 유의어. ❌ helpless(무력한): 유의어. ❌ exposed(노출된): 유사 의미.
det.tip: defenseless(무방비의) ↔ protected(보호받는). defense(방어) + less(없는) = 방어 없는.

questions.passage: Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, <u>ring</u> especially true in this context. "They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ring의 문맥적 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
ch: The phone began to ring loudly.
His warning rang true years later.
She wore a gold ring on her finger.
The children formed a ring around the tree.

det.korean: Andy Warhol의 말이 이 맥락에서 특히 진실처럼 들린다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'ring true'는 '진실되게 들리다'는 관용 표현. 본문과 동일한 용법. ❌ ①: '전화가 울리다' — 소리를 내다의 뜻. ❌ ③: '반지' — 명사 용법. ❌ ④: '원형' — 명사 용법.
det.tip: ring true = '진실처럼 들리다, 진정성이 있다'. ring은 '울리다(동사)', '반지(명사)', '원형(명사)' 등 다의어.

questions.passage: I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue because at the end of the day, you know, companies and governments can't ignore the interest of the consumers. At the same time, we also need to <u>pressure</u> governments and corporations to do the right thing.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 pressure의 영영풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: to make something smaller or tighter
to give financial support to an organization
to try to persuade or force someone to do something
to officially announce a decision or statement

det.korean: 정부와 기업이 옳은 일을 하도록 압력을 행사하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'pressure'는 '누군가에게 무언가를 하도록 설득하거나 강요하려고 시도하다'. ❌ ①: compress(압축하다)의 뜻. ❌ ②: fund(자금을 지원하다)의 뜻. ❌ ④: declare(선언하다)의 뜻.
det.tip: pressure(동사) = '압력을 가하다, 강요하다'. to try to persuade or force someone.

questions.passage: Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.
We are so (depend) __________ on plastic that it is nearly impossible to avoid it completely.

det.korean: 우리는 플라스틱에 너무 의존적이어서 그것을 완전히 피하는 것은 거의 불가능하다.
det.analysis: depend(동사) → dependent(형용사). 'be dependent on ~'은 '~에 의존하다'. 본문의 Dependence(명사)와 어근이 같은 형용사 형태.
det.tip: depend(동사) → dependent(형용사) → dependence(명사). be dependent on = depend on.

questions.passage: One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.
His paintings are full of (tender) __________ and warmth.

det.korean: 그의 그림은 부드러움과 따뜻함이 가득하다.
det.analysis: tender(형용사) → tenderness(명사). 'full of + 명사' 구조이므로 명사형이 필요. 본문에서도 tenderness로 사용됨.
det.tip: tender(부드러운, 형용사) → tenderness(부드러움, 명사). -ness는 형용사를 명사로 바꾸는 접미사.

questions.passage: One thing that art can do really well is to help us imagine how the world might be otherwise. Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it. I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a __________ rather than just reflect on what's wrong.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 잘못된 것을 깊이 생각하기보다는 밝은 희망을 표출하는 것이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① dark side
❌ ② harsh reality
❌ ③ lost cause
✅ ④ silver lining
✅ silver lining: '어두운 상황 속 밝은 면, 희망'. 'rather than just reflect on what's wrong'과 대조를 이룸. ❌ dark side(어두운 면): what's wrong과 유사해 대조 불가. ❌ harsh reality(냉혹한 현실): 부정적. ❌ lost cause(실패한 대의): 부정적.
det.tip: silver lining = '구름 뒤 은빛 테두리' → '어두운 상황 속 밝은 면'. Every cloud has a silver lining.

questions.passage: Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot resident, to create art that would highlight Port Talbot's dust problem. Owen believed that the area's children were facing serious health risks by playing in the dust coming from the local steel plant. Children are particularly __________ against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어린이들은 대기 오염에 특히 무방비 상태이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① defenseless
❌ ② indifferent
❌ ③ resistant
❌ ④ immune
✅ defenseless: '무방비의, 방어할 수 없는'. 어린이들이 호흡이 빨라서 더 많은 오염 물질을 들이마신다는 후속 근거와 일치. ❌ indifferent(무관심한): 어린이의 의지와 무관. ❌ resistant(저항력 있는): 반대 의미. ❌ immune(면역이 있는): 반대 의미.
det.tip: defenseless = defense(방어) + less(없는). against(~에 대해)와 함께 '~에 무방비인'.
